I will still do the wheat-maize rotation on all 30.4 mu, same as before. On my land, I do not like cutting fertilizer too much, because if yield drops, that loss is bigger than wasting a little input. I finished primary school, so I do look at what the dealer says and what neighbors with good fields do, but I mostly follow what has worked here in Quzhou. For wheat, I will use a good improved variety, put more fertilizer into the base, and keep 3 irrigations if water is normal: one after sowing or for winter moisture if needed, one at jointing, one at filling. Wheat is my steady crop, so I will not save money on nitrogen. For maize, I will plant hybrid seed because that pays better here, and I will keep fertilizer a little lower than wheat but still enough to push yield. Since I have well irrigation, I can give maize 2 waterings if rain is short. On this size of land, I think about yield first and labor second, so I will use machinery for rotary tillage and keep pesticide sprays on time rather than wait for the problem to get big.
